a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition: For every natural number m, assuming m is nonzero, if m ≥ 2 then there is no S1 system N with Boolean inputs and outputs satisfying both of the following conditions. (1) Its dependency relation has no directed path of positive length from any node back to itself, so even a self-loop is forbidden. There is an edge from i to j exactly when there exist two full state assignments agreeing at every node other than i, and a single Boolean input for which the update at j differs between the two assignments. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. (2) For every finite list of Boolean inputs, including the empty list, the output of N after starting from its own initial state and updating on the list from left to right equals the output of d26 m: it is true exactly when the number of true entries is divisible by m. Only the outputs must agree, not the internal states or updates. N has finitely many nodes as required by S1, but its individual node state types need not be finite."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition: For every natural number m, assuming m is nonzero, if m ≥ 2 then there is no S1 system N with Boolean inputs and outputs satisfying both of the following conditions. (1) Its dependency relation has no directed path of positive length from any node back to itself, so even a self-loop is forbidden. There is an edge from i to j exactly when there exist two full state assignments agreeing at every node other than i, and a single Boolean input for which the update at j differs between the two assignments. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. (2) For every finite list of Boolean inputs, including the empty list, the output of N after starting from its own initial state and updating on the list from left to right equals the output of d26 m: it is true exactly when the number of true entries is divisible by m. Only the outputs must agree, not the internal states or updates. N has finitely many nodes as required by S1, but its individual node state types need not be finite.

divergences.description: “Network” means a synchronous network with finitely many units, though each unit’s state type may be infinite. Dependence is tested on all state assignments, not just reachable ones. The claim does not cover infinite networks of unbounded depth.

The counter counts true inputs and outputs only whether the count is zero modulo m. A twin must match that Boolean output after every finite sequence, including the empty one; it need not report the full residue.

judgement.summary: With those model choices, the TARGET defines exactly the stated impossibility claim: it excludes every dependency cycle, including a self-loop, and requires one candidate twin to match at all finite lengths. The passage comparison is accurate as the author’s interpretation: Doerig et al. contrast feedforward and recurrent systems without explicitly defining the no-self-loop criterion, while Hanson and Walker describe self-dependence in the first component, which alone violates that criterion.
